business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L. 561-1 et seq.), Ordonnance n° 2017-821 du 5 mai 2017 relative au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, and EU AMLD5/6 directives

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Identification Form and Supporting Documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French Notary or Foreign Competent Authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French Tracfin, EU consolidated sanctions lists, UN sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and domestic French PEP register

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language with diacritical marks; no transliteration required as French uses Latin alphabet exclusively
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words reserved for public authorities (e.g., État, République, Ministère)
Names identical to or confusing with existing trademarks, company names, or public institutions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Président du Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection notice, followed by potential judicial review in the appropriate administrative court

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for non-regulated activities; virtual office addresses are permissible for SARL incorporation and ongoing compliance provided they meet French commercial substance requirements
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10% for routine pre-incorporation checks; higher for tax audits post-incorporation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market rate
Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border compliance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization if applicable (for foreign documents)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. governing the formation and governance of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); complemented by the general provisions of the Civil Code (Code civil), Articles 1832 to 1844-17.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the territorial district of the registered office, operating exclusively through the national business formalities portal Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises, administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création de société (standard creation/filing form) lodged electronically through the Guichet Unique portal; official incorporation is evidenced by the Kbis extract issued upon entry into the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), together with the certified statuts.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital: founders may fix capital at or above EUR 1.00. Subscribed cash contributions must be fully paid at incorporation and deposited within eight days of receipt into a blocked escrow account held by an approved credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary; the block certificate is filed with the registration dossier and funds are released only after the RCS/Kbis registration. In-kind contributions exceeding EUR 30,000 or representing more than half of the share capital require valuation by an appointed contributions auditor (commissaire aux apports) unless the shareholders unanimously waive this appointment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — The founders, holding 100% of the share capital, UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVE: 1. Confirmation of share subscription. Each subscriber's allocation is definitively accepted as set out in the subscription schedule; the manager is authorized to collect any final cash instalments and to secure escrow release upon registration. 2. Adoption of registered office. The company's seat is fixed at [address] and registered with the Commercial Court Registry; the manager may sign all occupancy consents and lease documents. 3. Appointment of management. Mr/Ms [Name] is appointed sole General Manager (Gérant) for the company's full statutory term, with full powers to bind the company, open bank accounts, and execute daily trading contracts. RESOLVED, approved and passed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and drafting of the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI trademark and business-name database (data.inpi.fr) for clearance; corporate lawyer or notary drafting the statuts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed company denomination against the INPI trademark register and local commercial names to verify availability. Instruct counsel to draft the statuts containing the legal form (SARL), corporate name, registered office, lasting period, corporate purpose limited to wholesale trade in whole and skimmed milk powder (ISIC 4633), share capital, management powers, and share transfer rules. Notarization is mandatory only if real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Name and domain availability search report
Draft statuts in the parties' agreed wording
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a prior conflicting right is identified through the INPI search, the shareholders select an alternative distinctive denomination and amend the statuts before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of paid-in share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved French credit institution, notary's office, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocking account in the name of the company being formed; each associate wires the subscribed cash amount; the bank or notary issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital blocking certificate) declaring that the funds are irrevocably blocked until presentation of the Kbis extract, at which point the funds are released to the company's operational account.
required_dossiers: Final or near-final version of the statuts
Signed cash subscription statements for each associate
Bank KYC forms, identity documents and source-of-funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses or delays, obtain a formal written refusal and transfer the deposit to a notary's escrow account within the statutory 8-day window; any late deposit restarts the certification process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the statutory legal notice (avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcements newspaper (Journal d'annonces légales) expressly authorized in the département of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to the Journal d'annonces légales the notice of incorporation containing the company's name, SARL form, registered office address, concise corporate purpose, share capital, duration, and identity of the Gérant. The publisher validates the notice against the statuts and issues the attestation de parution to be appended to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the signed statuts
Identity and address details of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal queries the wording as incomplete, republish the corrected notice and obtain a supplementary publication certificate, with costs borne by the founder responsible for the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic lodgment of the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with onward transmission to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP and other competent administrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the portal, complete the SARL creation declaration (standard e-form M0 or equivalent), identify the Gérant and beneficial owners, attach all mandatory scanned documents, pay the filing fee online, and submit. The INPI portal validates completeness and sends the dossier to the Greffe of the registered office district for legal control and registration.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (PDF or legally recognized electronic signature)
Bank or notary capital deposit certificate
Legal notice publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Copy of the Gérant's valid photo ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried or rejected, correct the flagged elements and re-submit within the legal rectification window (approximately 15 days); if the deadline lapses, a fresh application and new fee are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, Kbis certificate issuance and ancillary statutory notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court); INSEE for SIREN/SIRET allocation; DGFiP for corporate tax elections.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legal regularity of the dossier, records the company in the RCS, assigns the RCS/SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and issues the official Kbis extract — the company's statutory incorporation certificate. Concurrently, the manager files the justified address occupation certificate and files the corporate income tax regime election with the local DGFiP; the company automatically receives its tax and social security identification references.
required_dossiers: Attestation de jouissance des locaux (occupancy certificate for the registered office)
Kbis application receipt or pending registration notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration, the Gérant may petition the President of the Commercial Court for a judicial review of the refusal; alternatively, correct the identified irregularities and resubmit a complete file with the renewed fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) under the functional supervision of the Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) for food business operator registration and dairy import/wholesale controls; Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for facilities-based environmental admissions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registre sanitaire / déclaration d'entreprise alimentaire (sanitary registration as a food business operator) for the wholesale distribution of whole and skimmed milk powder, together with the SIVEP/SIGAL import notification registration where third-country-origin goods are brought into the EU; any physically operated cold-storage warehouse requires the ICPE environmental operating authorization as applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), Ministry of Ecological Transition, Territoriaux and Prefecture services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pure wholesale trading is not subject to full cultural impact assessment. Physical cold-storage of dairy products falls under the ICPE framework (Code de l'environnement R.511-9), typically rubric 2925 (refrigerated warehouses) under the simple declaration (déclaration) regime; facilities exceeding declaration thresholds are subject to the registration (enregistrement) regime. A full environmental impact study (étude d'impact) is required only where the authorization (autorisation) regime is triggered by installed capacity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: connection to municipal sewers requires compliance with prefectural discharge limits (Code de la santé publique art. L.1331-1 et seq.): BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 5.5-8.5; without public sewer, a ZDEC/ZDET off-site or on-site treatment plan applies. Air emissions: sealed powder conveying and filling lines with fugitive dust extraction limited to ≤ 50 mg/m³ in exhaust streams per ministerial decree; compliance with EU F-Gas Regulation No 517/2014 for refrigeration leakage testing and refrigerant passports. Waste: milk-powder residues tracked via bordereau de suivi des déchets (BSD) with licensed waste haulers and energy-recovery routes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Commission de sécurité for warehouses and workspaces under the Labor Code R.4227 series, including extinguishers, detection, egress, and annual drill records; structural load inspection evidenced by a certified engineer's attestation de résistance des planchers validating racking and palletized powder load thresholds; workplace health and safety clearance through CARSAT registration, establishment of the DUERP risk assessment document, worker medical surveillance, and CSE documentation where staff thresholds are met.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; taxpayer portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; business registration portal (Guichet Unique): formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and indirect duties: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), www.douane.gouv.fr; EU-wide VAT number validation: European Commission VIES portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL (including 100% non-resident ownership): (1) file the formation dossier through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, a single INPI-operated electronic counter; certified corporate documents of the foreign parent and the appointed gérant are attached; (2) INSEE allocates the 9-digit SIREN and the 14-digit SIRET upon registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); (3) DGFiP automatically allocates the intra-Community VAT number (format FR + 2 control digits + 9 digits, VIES-validated) after validation of the début d'activité; the VAT number appears in the Sirene directory; (4) obtain a French EORI number (FR + SIREN) from DGDDI for customs operations; (5) a non-established foreign trader without a French fixed establishment may obtain a direct French VAT number from the DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises or the Direction des impôts des non-résidents) under the standalone non-resident registration procedure. The SARL must file its first periodic CA3 VAT return from the month of its first taxable transaction and appoint a fiscal representative only when required for non-established operators.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — default regime is Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at the standard 25% rate, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit if the SARL qualifies (turnover below EUR 10,000,000, capital fully paid up, at least 75% held by individuals or qualifying entities, Article 219-I-b CGI). Under the territoriality principle (Article 209-I CGI and BOFIP-IS-GPE-20-20-20), profits realized through a French establishment are taxable in France while profits of a distinct foreign permanent establishment are exempt, absent a rare worldwide (consolidated) election under Article 209 E CGI. The SARL is a French tax resident under Article 209-A CGI; distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to withholding tax under Article 119 bis 2 CGI at treaty rates. The SARL is not located in a tax-exempt zone as standard French territory applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms: (1) pass-through election under Article 239 bis AA CGI for qualifying SARLs (capital continuously held at least 50% by individuals or by an IR-subject company, 50 employees or fewer, and annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10,000,000 for goods traders) for a limited irrevocable period of 5 fiscal years, renewable; (2) VAT group (assujetti unique) election under Article 267 C CGI for closely linked entities with financial, economic and organizational interdependence; (3) option under Article 260 C CGI to waive the franchise en base de TVA and apply normal VAT rules where turnover remains below the statutory thresholds; (4) options under Articles 260 A and 260 B CGI for VAT treatment of specific real estate and financial services, not relevant to dairy commodity trading; (5) no elective mechanism for hybrid mismatches: the ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules (Articles 212 bis, 209-0 B, 239 octies A CGI) apply automatically and mandatorily.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.registration_timeline_comment: VAT registration is immediate upon exceedance of the franchise threshold or upon the first import; the EORI number must be procured before the first customs declaration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA), governed by Articles 256 to 277 A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by DGFiP for returns and by DGDDI for VAT at importation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA (Articles 293 B and 293 B quinquies CGI; 2025 revalued thresholds): for sales of goods (ventes de marchandises) the normal threshold is EUR 91,900 and the upper tolerance limit is EUR 105,000; for services EUR 39,100 / EUR 43,400. A wholesale dairy milk powder trader exceeds the goods threshold and must register for VAT from the transaction exceeding the upper tolerance, or immediately upon exceeding the normal threshold where prior-year turnover already exceeded it; in practice the SARL registers with the SIE before its first taxable supply or import. Non-established foreign suppliers are required to register regardless of threshold when making taxable supplies in France, and import VAT is due at clearance unless the company holds a DGFiP authorization to self-assess import VAT on its CA3 return.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France operates a 'data-hub' e-invoicing model with no Italian-style real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Under the 2024 Finance Act (postponed calendar): from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices and large/mid-size companies must issue e-invoices; from 1 September 2027 small/micro companies must issue e-invoices. E-invoices are issued via a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the state-run Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); formats must comply with EN 16931 (Factur-X, UBL, CII); transmission and e-reporting of transaction and payment data to the PPF occurs normally within one business day of issuance. Cross-border B2B supplies (intra-EU and extra-EU) are subject to e-reporting; B2G invoicing remains on Chorus Pro; API specifications for PPF/PDP interconnection are published by DGFiP. Sanctions under Article 1737 CGI apply per non-compliant invoice (up to EUR 15 per invoice, with annual caps from EUR 15,000 to EUR 60,000 by company size).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération) applies to definitive exports of goods outside the EU customs territory under Article 262-I-1° CGI: sales of whole and skimmed milk powder to non-EU buyers qualify when the seller proves physical removal of the goods from the EU within the accounting period and holds transport documentation in its name or that of its customer. The French SARL should be named as exporter of record (exportateur) on the DAU/ECS customs declaration. Intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered customers are exempt, not zero-rated, under Article 262 ter I CGI, subject to valid EU VAT number, EC Sales List (DEB/DEPS) filing and customer VIES validation. Under Article 262-I-2° CGI, directly related offshore services (handling, transport, logistics) supporting the exported goods may also be zero-rated. Domestic sales of dairy products for human consumption attract the reduced 5.5% rate (Article 278 bis CGI) but exports always benefit from 0% or exemption, with full input VAT recovery via the periodic CA3 return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: French DAU/ECS declaration (or the export declaration where the seller is exporter of record) validated by DGDDI, showing the SARL's French EORI and VAT number, HS codes 0402.10 (whole milk powder) or 0402.10/0402.91 (skimmed milk powder), the exit customs office and the date of exit from EU customs territory.

Bill of Lading (or CMR, air waybill or multimodal transport document): evidencing physical exit from the EU, with shipment route, port/airport of exit, consignee and cargo description matching the commercial invoice and customs declaration.

Inward Remittance Certificate: bank payment confirmation (SWIFT MT103 cash transfer or MT700 documentary credit), or the French bank credit advice / attestation de domiciliation bancaire showing receipt of export proceeds in the SARL's French bank account within the commercial payment cycle.

Supporting commercial evidence: signed export sales contract or purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin (EUR.1 where required), and, for intra-Community exempt supplies, VIES validation evidence of the customer's EU VAT number and the recapitulative DEB/DEPS statement.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP applies an extended 10-year reassessment right for VAT where export substantiation is concerned (Article L176 LPF), against the ordinary 3-year window (Article L169 LPF). If the export documentation bundle is missing or inconsistent, the zero-rating is clawed back: VAT is reassessed at 20% on the sales price, plus monthly late interest (intérêt de retard at 0.2% per month), plus penalties: 40% for bad-faith understatement (Article 1729-a CGI) and 80% for abusive or fraudulent maneuvers (Article 1729-b CGI), including fictitious exports and carousel-type arrangements. The abuse-of-law procedure (Article L64 LPF, 80% penalty) and joint liability under Article 283-4 CGI may apply where the supplier knew or should have known of customer-side fraud. Criminal exposure under Article 1741 CGI reaches EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment (aggravated fraud: EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years); customs fraud under Articles 414-415 of the Code des douanes attracts penalties of one to three times the evaded duties, confiscation of goods and vehicles, and imprisonment of 3 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) – national central bank, authority for balance-of-payments statistics and the Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds (DTF) reporting system; exchange-control policy coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique. The European Central Bank (ECB) exercises monetary sovereignty over the euro.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. France is an IMF Article VIII member; capital movements are liberalised under Articles 63-65 TFEU; the euro (EUR) is a fully convertible EU currency. No prior exchange-control approval, license, conversion quota, or repatriation restriction applies to trade payments, shareholder capital injections, loan disbursements, or profit remittances by a French SARL engaged in ISIC 4633 dairy wholesale. The compliance architecture is limited to: (i) statistical DTF reporting of every cross-border transfer to/from France of EUR 10,000 or above per transaction (Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.152-1 and R.152-1 to R.152-2-2), filed electronically on the BdF ONE portal – normally discharged automatically by the French instructing bank, or within 20 working days by the French-resident account holder where the transfer bypasses a French intermediary; (ii) EU and national financial sanctions screening of counterparties; (iii) foreign-direct-investment prior-authorisation only for sensitive sectors under CMF Article L.151-3 – not applicable to raw milk powder wholesale (ISIC 4633/NAICS 424430); and (iv) corporate-law and tax formalities on profit distribution: a valid shareholders' decision complying with Code de commerce Article L.232-11 (positive distributable profit, net-asset test), followed by dividend withholding at 30% PFU for non-resident individuals (treaty-reduced as applicable) or 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Article 119 ter CGI, subject to the 5% holding and 2-year minimum thresholds). No BdF or DG Trésor clearance is required for any such remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR, no repatriation deadline, and no holding-period requirement on export proceeds. A French SARL may retain foreign currency indefinitely in an authorised foreign-currency account (compte en devises), use such balances directly for supplier settlements, or convert them via spot/forward contracts. The sole obligation is the DTF statistical declaration for any cross-border fund movement of EUR 10,000 or more; when the export proceeds are received into a French bank account, the receiving bank files the declaration as statutory intermediary. If proceeds are collected in a non-French account and thereafter remitted to France, the SARL itself must ensure the DTF is filed with the BdF within 20 working days.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account (EUR + major currencies), dedicated Commodity Trade Finance / Documentary Credit desk
Operational Current Account, EUR/USD/NZD foreign-currency sub-accounts, Trade Finance and FX/Treasury execution lines

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (via Crédit Agricole regional bank or LCL)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account and Standby/Commercial Letter of Credit facilities (UCP 600)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE / Natixis SA (Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne networks)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account; limited SME commodity-finance appetite

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale / CIC (Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account, SEPA and SWIFT payment rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – Conditionally Viable for operational disbursements only; non-viable for escrow or trade-finance functions. ACPR-registered French/EEA electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Manager.one, Treezor-based platforms) are acceptable for SEPA CT/SCT, supplier payouts, and multi-currency FX conversion, but none provide commercial LC issuance, standby LC, bank guarantees, or commodity pre-finance. Offshore non-EEA EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business with non-French IBANs) are treated as heightened-risk by French tier-1 banks and ACPR inspectors; they may be used only as supplementary collection channels, never as the primary treasury anchor or as holder of equity escrow funds. Legal constraint: EMIs are not credit institutions (no deposit-taking licence, no Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution cover), so escrowed equity capital and client trade deposits must remain with an ACPR-licensed credit institution subject to the French deposit-blocking regime for SARL incorporation capital.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is the prevailing tier-1 policy and is mandatory for the gérant (managing director) and each natural-person UBO whose identity is not already registered in the EU/EEA financial system; this reflects the customer-due-diligence duty under CMF Article L.561-5. Remote video onboarding is accepted by a minority of networks (BNP Paribas digital onboarding, Société Générale 'pro' video-KYC) only where all signatories are EEA residents or hold a French digital identity (France Identité / Loi 2020-901 eID). For a non-resident shareholder-director, the standard compliant routes are: (i) in-person interview at a French branch with original passport, proof of address, and original corporate documents; or (ii) signature certification at a French consulate or notary plus a supervised video interview, with apostilled corporate documents. Budget 10-25 business days for the 4-eyes (compliance + risk) review; a French-resident legal proxy may manage the file but does not substitute for UBO identification and interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly non-resident ownership of the SARL with limited apparent French economic substance (shell-company red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified KBIS extract and notarised articles of association; (ii) full UBO chain to natural persons filed at the INPI Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs; (iii) apostilled passports and utility-bill proof of address for each UBO; (iv) French registered-office lease; (v) substance evidence – French payroll, professional indemnity insurance, signed supply and distribution contracts with French/EU dairy counterparties; (vi) reference letter and 12 months of statements from the shareholder's home-country primary bank; (vii) audited or professionally prepared opening accounts and a 3-year business plan with transaction-throughput projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Routed third-party payments through brokers, tolling processors, or non-invoiced intermediaries in dairy commodity flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contractual chain: master purchase and sale contracts, commission and brokerage agreements, final trade invoices, warehouse receipts, SGS/ALS inspection certificates, bills of lading, customs declarations (DAU/DELTA-G), and a structured payment-flow chart; written undertaking to settle only with direct contractual counterparties; where split payments are unavoidable, a documented commercial justification and bankability memo submitted before execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-margin wire activity with tight invoice-value variance (commodity round-tripping / trade-based money-laundering typology)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Verifiable per-transaction trail: pre-shipment inspection certificates, weighbridge delivery confirmations, customs entry records, marine insurance cover notes, and a reconciliation report matching each MT103, commercial invoice, bill of lading quantity, and contract reference; formal adoption of a 'one invoice – one payment' policy; engagement of an external audit firm to certify the trade cycle quarterly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Holdings of non-EEA foreign-currency balances or connection to crypto-adjacent treasury flows (sanctions / proliferation-financing exposure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial justification for foreign-currency accounts (e.g., NZD-denominated supplier invoices); board-approved treasury policy expressly prohibiting crypto-assets and anonymous payment channels; live real-time EU/OFAC sanctions-screening output for all counterparties; confirmation of automatic DTF reporting via the French bank; commitment to maintain any foreign-currency account solely at an ACPR-licensed bank or a top-100 global bank with a French branch.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or shareholder-loan injections must arrive via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT where the shareholder is EEA-resident) with an accurate purpose code and narration. For statutory capital: the funds must first be deposited at a licensed bank or with a notary before RCS registration (Code de commerce Article L.223-7 – at least 20% of each in-cash share paid at subscription; balance within 5 years); upon immatriculation, the depository releases the funds to the SARL's operational account. The MT103 must reference the BdF DTF purpose category 'Investissements directs – prises de participation' (shareholder loans: category 'Crédits financiers'), with narration citing the articles of association or the EGM capital-increase resolution. Verification protocol: the receiving French bank requires the attestation de dépôt de fonds or notarial confirmation of deposit; the bank files the DTF automatically where the inbound amount equals or exceeds EUR 10,000; for transfers from a third-country bank, the complete originator chain and ultimate-beneficiary references must be provided. If the SARL is the indirect recipient via a foreign treasury account, a full chain-of-title schedule must accompany the onward remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 open-account settlement to EU and third-country dairy suppliers (e.g., New Zealand, Ireland, Germany, Netherlands) with the purpose-code category 'Paiements de marchandises' and invoice/contract references in fields 70-71A; executed in EUR via SEPA/TARGET2 or in USD/NZD via BNP Paribas/Société Générale correspondent banks in New York/Wellington, with FX trades cut before 10:00 CET for same-day value; (ii) Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 issued by the French opening bank (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole CIB) in favour of the offshore supplier, available by sight payment or deferred acceptance, covering whole/skimmed milk powder shipments; LC issuance requires margin collateralisation typically 10-30% for a newly onboarded SARL; (iii) Standby LC / demand guarantee under ISP98 to collateralise prepayments to suppliers; (iv) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst, EUR 100,000 per-transaction ceiling) for European suppliers requiring real-time settlement; (v) consolidation of all outbound flows through a single French treasury account to preserve an automatic, complete DTF audit trail. All outbound transfers of EUR 10,000 or more are DTF-declared by the French bank without client action; no regulatory approval is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (Achat/Vente à Terme de Devises) – deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/NZD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY outright forwards up to 24-month tenors under an ISDA or FBF master agreement
FX Swap (Swap de Change) – short-dated EUR/USD and EUR/NZD swaps to bridge timing mismatches between LC negotiations and supplier disbursements
Outright FX Option / Collar (Option de Change / Tunnel) – zero-premium EUR-call / foreign-currency-put collars to fix budget rates on USD and NZD payables
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) – for economically hedging long-term USD/GBP shareholder loans or capital-lease obligations

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permitted solely for non-convertible emerging-market counterparty currencies (e.g., EGP, NGN, PKR) via the French bank's offshore NDF desk; unavailable and unnecessary for EUR crosses because EUR/USD, EUR/NZD, and EUR/GBP are freely convertible deliverable markets

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays applicable to dairy commodity trading. Eligible SMEs may apply the reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit, subject to turnover and ownership conditions. The Research Tax Credit (CIR) and Innovation Tax Credit (CII) are available to qualifying research and innovation expenditures, but a commodity trading SARL would rarely meet the substantive R&D test.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited (annual deduction cap: EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding that amount)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) and required annex forms (notably 2058-ES, 2058-C, 2058-A, 2031); electronic filing is mandatory via EFI/EDI professional portals or the impots.gouv.fr EDI service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly instalment payments (acomptes) and one final settlement (solde) in the following year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, the statutory filing deadline is 3 May of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code (ISIC 4633 equivalent 4630Z/4649Z), registered office, legal form, tax office, manager identification and corporate address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French permanent establishment of a foreign head-office, provide the foreign company's identity, country, and French tax agent details; use the PE's SIRET-specific address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover, other operating income, purchases and inventories, external charges, staff costs, depreciation, provisions, other operating expenses, financial income/expenses, exceptional items, and net accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the French PE under arm's length principles; exclude income of the foreign head-office; separately disclose intercompany commodity purchases and sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year deficit for carryback election (option pour le report en arrière), prior-year deficits carried forward to reduce taxable income, and any loss carryforward usage within the annual cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses attributable to the French PE may be carried forward; losses of the foreign head-office or other foreign establishment may not be offset in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D – Calcul de l'impôt sur les sociétés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after add-backs of non-deductible expenses; application of 25% standard rate or 15% SME reduced rate; deduction of instalments already paid; resulting final corporate tax liability and, if applicable, 3.3% social contribution on profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply DTA rules limiting French taxing rights over PE profit; reflect foreign tax credits only where the foreign tax was paid on French-source income under a treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E – Réductions et crédits d'impôt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (recherche, innovation, foreign tax credit, tax at source) and deductions reducing the net corporate income tax; attach accompanying forms (2069-RCI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is limited to the amount of French tax attributable to the same foreign-source income; DTA residence certificate must evidence the foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F – Transactions with non-resident related parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of transactions carried out with foreign related companies: nature, amount, and transfer pricing method (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, profit split); confirmation that TP documentation is available.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French PE must maintain contemporaneous documentation if the consolidated group tolerance of EUR 400 million gross turnover/assets is met; below the threshold, provide a concise written benchmark analysis upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box G – Distributions and withholding on dividends
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts of dividends decided during the fiscal year, identity of each shareholder and share of paid amounts; the form marks the application of withholding tax to non-resident beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) establishing entitlement to treaty reduction; for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, provide a beneficial ownership declaration on Form 2562-TB and prove 10% direct shareholding held for two years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the assessed tax (10% after formal notice) under CGI Art. 1728; late payment interest: 0.20% per month under CGI Art. 1727; deliberate misstatement or fraud: 40% penalty under CGI Art. 1729, and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law under CGI Art. 1729-0. Directors/executives may be jointly liable under Article L. 267 of the French Tax Procedures Book if the company is unable to pay the penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The statutory 30% withholding tax on dividends is withheld by the paying French SARL at source. Relief is not automatic: before payment, the non-resident shareholder must furnish an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction and, for EU/EEA exempt entities, a signed beneficial ownership declaration (Cerfa 2562-TB) demonstrating 10% direct shareholding for two years. The payer applies the reduced DTA rate through the annual dividend filing or the shareholder seeks a refund from the Local Tax Directorate (DDFiP) within the statutory time limit (normally 31 December of the second calendar year following the distribution).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax rate is 33.33% for payments of patents, know-how, trademarks and similar IP to non-residents; under an applicable DTA the rate is commonly reduced to 0% or 10%, and the EU Interest-Royalties Directive may eliminate withholding for associated EU companies (25% direct shareholding for two years). Interest: domestic French law generally applies no withholding tax on arm's length interest paid by a French debtor to non-bank non-resident lenders, except where the lender is a controlling shareholder and the interest is recharacterised as a hidden dividend; treaty rates commonly reduce any residual WHT to nil or to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (gross turnover or gross balance-sheet total of the French entity or the worldwide group); below this threshold, basic contemporaneous documentation must nevertheless be prepared and produced at the tax auditor's request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulation comparable to common-law offshore centres. However, under Article L. 64 of the French Tax Procedures Book the abuse-of-law doctrine permits disregard of artificial arrangements lacking genuine commercial substance; the OECD principal purpose test under treaties further denies tax benefits if obtaining treaty relief was a principal purpose. A French SARL engaged in raw milk powder trade must demonstrate actual management decisions, physical office or storage facilities, staff, commercial correspondence, logistics control, and real intra-group substance, particularly when claiming DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful under-declaration of dairy sales, use of fictitious invoices for raw-milk-powder purchases, concealment of rebates or cash payments, or deliberately shifting profit to a non-resident related supplier while leaving the French SARL without economic substance and underlying trade performance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: 80% fraud penalty under CGI Art. 1729-0 and late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Criminal: under CGI Art. 1741, a fine of up to EUR 3,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 7 years for the natural persons organising the evasion; the court may also order closure of the business, publication of the judgement, and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In cases of fraudulent misstatement or concealment of assets, managers may be declared personally liable for the SARL's tax debt and penalties under Article L. 267 LPF, thereby piercing the corporate veil. Travel bans, asset freezes and judicial supervision are common during criminal investigation; conviction may result in imprisonment and a professional ban on acting as a company director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a French SARL with no genuine business activity, staff, premises, warehouse capacity or management authority, used only as an intermediary to convert foreign dairy trading margins into treaty-protected French dividends, or to create a paper French presence for tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where the French tax authority exercises the abuse-of-law doctrine under LPF Art. L. 64, the artificial arrangement is set aside; the taxpayer must bear a 80% penalty on the resulting under-assessed tax, interest is computed at 0.20% per month, and all DTA benefits may be denied. Additional criminal prosecution for fraud is possible where intent is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director of a sham company is exposed to joint and several liability for the enterprise's tax and penalties under Article L. 267 LPF if he or she used the structure to avoid or defeat tax collection. Courts may impose a ban on managing commercial enterprises and a prohibition from leaving French territory for the duration of the criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a non-arm's length price for imported whole-milk-powder from a related supplier or re-invoicing services at inflated fees, so that the French SARL realises a below-market gross margin or recurring losses, while the related offshore entity captures all profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may adjust the transfer price to the arm's length level and reallocate profit to France; the reassessment is increased by a 40% penalty under CGI Art. 1729 in cases of deliberate or negligent omission, and to 80% if payments are made to a judicial non-cooperative state or if abuse of law is found. Late-payment interest and the 3.3% social contribution on reassessed profit also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When a manager signs the corporate income tax return containing manipulated transfer-pricing figures and knowingly participates in the scheme, personal liability may arise under criminal tax law and under Article L. 267 LPF for debts owed by the company; a sentence may include imprisonment up to 5 years for customs or false-document offences in cross-border transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing cash proceeds, wire transfers or SWIFT documentary credits for raw-milk-powder consignments without identifying the ultimate beneficial owner, bypassing customer due diligence with shell sales companies, or using an intermediary's account to conceal the real origin or destination of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable under Articles 324-1 and 324-2 of the French Criminal Code by 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine; aggravated laundering (participation in a criminal organisation, habitual laundering, use of the financial system) raises the penalty to 10 years and EUR 750,000. Tracfin notification failures may trigger separate administrative fines and confiscation of goods and bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL's legal fiction does not protect directors when they order or tolerate the use of false invoices or foreigners' shell accounts; the directors are prosecutable as principals or accomplices. During the investigation, the court may order travel bans, seizure of passports, freezing of bank assets, and, upon conviction, imprisonment and prohibition from professional activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming a reduced withholding tax rate under a French tax treaty without obtaining a genuine Tax Residence Certificate or while the real beneficiary is a different person resident in a non-treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The application of the reduced withholding rate is revoked; the tax administration collects the difference between the treaty rate and the statutory 30% withholding, together with interest for late payment; a fine of 80% is added for intentional misrepresentation or abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the Form 2562-TB knowing the identity of the ultimate recipient to be false can be held jointly liable for the unpaid withholding tax and may be subject to criminal penalties for tax fraud; travel restrictions may be ordered to guarantee the investigation.
